name: ripple-distortion
title: Ripple Distortion
description: A full-bleed grayscale landscape where the pointer pushes water-like ripples that distort the image and slowly fade, tinted faintly violet.
use: A landing or hero image needs a tactile, pointer-reactive surface that invites play.
avoid: It needs WebGL and a sized parent, and the hover effect is inert on touch devices.
a11y: The canvas has no label or description, so the photograph and the effect stay invisible to screen readers. (keyboard: n-a, labels: none, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A full-bleed grayscale photograph of snowy mountains over a sea of cloud, cropped to fill the stage. Where the pointer passes, round blobs bulge with a pale violet sheen and smeared, stretched detail; a faint caption sits near the bottom edge.
behaves: Moving the pointer spawns ripples that grow and swirl the picture beneath them, each fading over a few seconds. Clicking pushes a stronger pulse, and the effect stills itself if reduced motion is requested.
customise: Image source, brush size, strength, swirl, rings, spread, fade, dispersion, glint, tint and quality are props; trigger, click strength and enable toggle too.
weight: heavy: A WebGL render loop draws a displacement pass and a composite pass every frame.
demo: Grayscale mountain-and-cloud photo with caption 'Move to disturb the water'.
issues: The default grayscale setting flattens the source photo to grey unless you turn it off.
polishWhy: Rich, smooth water warp that reads instantly; the violet tint is subtle and well judged.
